questions.q: Define 'perseverance' in the context of pursuing a long-term dream, using one phrase from the mother's letter that illustrates it.
questions.a: Perseverance is continuing to work toward a goal despite obstacles; the phrase "small, steady steps" from the letter illustrates it. A wrong answer like "never giving up" without textual evidence shows the student cannot anchor the definition in the text, a board-exam requirement.

questions.q: Explain in your own words how the mother describes her and the father's role as a support network for the daughter. Why does she use the metaphor of a 'safety net'?
questions.a: The mother describes them as a constant, non-judgmental backup who will catch the daughter if she fails, allowing her to take risks. The 'safety net' metaphor means they provide emotional security so failure isn't fatal. A wrong answer focusing only on financial support misses the emotional and motivational dimension central to the text.

questions.q: The mother advises: "Choose a mountain you can climb today, not the one you see in pictures." Apply the concept of realistic goal-setting to explain what this means for a student who wants to be a cricketer but has never played organized sports.
questions.a: It means the student should first join a local academy (achievable step) rather than dreaming only of the IPL (distant picture). Steps: 1) Identify current skill level (beginner). 2) Set immediate goal: learn basics at academy. 3) Measure progress monthly. 4) Adjust goal as skills grow. A wrong answer suggesting "practice hard and you'll make it" ignores the 'realistic' part — board exams require SMART goal breakdown.

questions.q: Compare how perseverance and support networks function differently in the letter. Use two distinct textual references to show that one is internal (daughter's action) and the other external (parents' action).
questions.a: Perseverance is internal: "you must walk the path yourself" — daughter's sustained effort. Support network is external: "we will hold the lantern" — parents providing guidance. A wrong answer that blends them as "help from others" fails to distinguish agency (perseverance) from environment (support), a common board-level confusion.

questions.q: Evaluate whether the mother's advice on realistic goal-setting might discourage big dreams. Defend your view using the letter's overall message about 'conviction and sacrifice'.
questions.a: No, it doesn't discourage big dreams; it structures them. The letter says "dreams are built brick by brick" — realistic goals are the bricks. Conviction keeps the vision; sacrifice is the daily effort. A wrong answer saying "yes, it limits dreams" misreads the text's balance between vision and practicality, losing marks for lack of textual synthesis.

questions.q: Write a 50-word letter from the daughter to her mother, demonstrating she has internalized all three values: perseverance, support network, and realistic goal-setting.
questions.a: A strong answer: "Ma, I've joined the district cricket academy (realistic goal). It's tough — 5 a.m. practice, sore muscles — but I'll persist (perseverance). Knowing you and Baba cheer from the stands makes every fall bearable (support network). I'll update you monthly. Love." A poor answer missing any one value shows incomplete integration of the three concepts.
